messages:
maria-ops: Heads up — after yesterday's geo-weight shift (APAC -> EU primary for a few VIPs) we saw a spike of 5xx errors from model-serving in eu-west-1 starting ~08:12 UTC. GPU queues ballooned and a lot of pods reported connection resets. Symptoms look like egress/NAT resource pressure rather than model OOMs.

sam-infra: saw the same. conntrack logs show a ton of entries and nat-gateway CPU hitting 95%. On the nodes we're seeing `iptables: conntrack: table full` in dmesg.

asha-sre: timeline: weight change pushed at 08:10, traffic ramped in ~120s, error spike at 08:12. Affected customers mostly low-latency RT routes that pin to region by policy.

kevin-runtime: confirming — model-serving pods didn't spike memory or GPU utilization dramatically. Instead, request latencies went high waiting on new connections; many short-lived connections. Looks like we're creating a ton of ephemeral TCP sessions per request (no connection reuse).

robin-eng: quick log excerpt from the edge router showing resets and TCP RSTs:
```
2025-11-09T08:12:05Z router-1 edge: tcp_reset src=10.12.8.45 dst=52.14.9.120 sport=34567 dport=443
2025-11-09T08:12:08Z kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
```

sam-infra: immediate mitigation we did: added two NAT instances to the eu pool and bumped conntrack max on the nodes. That reduced immediate errors but the root cause is still the abrupt traffic shift.

maria-ops: long term discussion — we need a safer rollback/failover policy for geo weight changes. Current strategy is too binary: change weight -> global bang. Need staged ramp + prewarm egress.

asha-sre: proposals: 1) implement staged geo ramp (10/30/60/100) with 2–5 minute windows and health-probe gating, 2) prewarm per-region egress (reserve small SNAT pool or ephemeral ports), 3) make router use persistent multiplexed connections to backend clusters.

kevin-runtime: +1 on multiplexing. If we can move client->edge long-lived TCP/HTTP2 and reuse backend connections (pooling to model-serving), ephemeral port consumption drops by >10x for many workloads. Also consider changing keepalive defaults on SDKs/SDK proxies.

sam-infra: technical constraints: NAT instances cost money when scaled; conntrack tuning helps but has limits. We can switch to per-region egress proxies (sidecar'ing a pool of egress proxies per AZ) so connection counts are aggregated. That's medium effort but fits our infra model.

robin-eng: GPU capacity part — while this incident was egress-driven, we saw queues on the GPU workers because requests were stuck in TCP handshake/slow path. That led to some autoscaler triggers because pods looked busy. We should add a backpressure signal from the router so we don't spin GPUs up just because egress is congested.

maria-ops: action items: sam to prototype per-region egress proxy (short-lived) + conntrack tuning doc; kevin to add a runtime ticket for connection pooling and keepalive defaults; robin to add router-side backpressure metric and a gate for the autoscaler; asha to own the geo weight ramp runbook.

sam-infra: immediate run commands we used:
```
# check conntrack
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
sudo watch -n1 "ss -s | grep estab"
# bump conntrack (temp):
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

asha-sre: notes on DNS TTLs — we tried lowering TTL to 30s to speed failover, but that increased churn and amplified the problem during the ramp. For staged ramps we should keep TTL moderate (60–120s) and rely on weight windows rather than super-low TTLs.

kevin-runtime: retry guidance: SDKs were retrying aggressively which increased connection churn. Need safer retry + jitter + circuit-breaker at the SDK level. I'll sketch a default policy: 2 retries with exponential backoff, per-host connection pooling enabled.

robin-eng: cost tradeoffs: prewarming NAT or adding persistent egress proxies has recurring cost. But compare that to the cost of overprovisioning GPUs because of false autoscaler signals — could be worse. I'll run a cost projection comparing a steady small NAT reserve vs. burst GPU allocation for typical customer traffic patterns.

maria-ops: timeline for items? prefer prototypes in 2 weeks; runbook + staged ramp enabled behind a feature flag in 1 month. Also schedule a chaos test to simulate weight shifts against SNAT-limited env.

deploy-bot: deployment notice: conntrack-bump config applied to eu nodes at 08:22 UTC (change id: deploy/9943). Rollback available.

sam-infra: I'll post my prototype repo link once the per-region egress proxy PoC is up. For now we should add a short checklist to oncall runbook: "if geo weight ramp causes 5xx spike -> check conntrack -> scale NAT -> consider roll back weight to previous window".

asha-sre: agreed. Also add dashboard panels: conntrack usage, nat gateway CPU, TCP resets per router, router queued requests, gpu-pod-ready-queue-length.

maria-ops: thanks everyone — good catch. We'll reconvene after PoCs. For the incident doc I'll paste the timeline and mitigation steps into incidents/ and link back here. :white_check_mark:
